The efficacy of penicillin and diethylcarbamazin (DEC) in preventing acute adenolymphagitis (ADL; attacks) was evaluated in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study in 150 persons who had experienced at least two episodes of ADL within the previous 12 months.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of affected-limb-care with oral penicillin and diethylcarbamzine (DEC) prophylaxis was found to be the most efficacious in reducing the incidence of acute adenolymhangitis during bancroften filariasis, but that affected-limb care alone also helped to reduce its frequency.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the affected-limb self-care programme, combined with oral penicillin prophphylaxis (with or without the additional benefit of DEC), is highly effective in preventing ADL attacks in people with lymphatic filariases.
